mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-over-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a sustained return of consumer activity, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed trend.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility approaches the -25% baseline threshold, it signals a critical mass of people returning to work, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation visits during lunch breaks and after hours, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES crosses -25% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks, or even declines.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests a broader return to urban centers and daily commutes. This combined effect will lead to a significant uplift in RETAIL_REC as more people are physically present in commercial areas, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite continued increases in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, RETAIL_REC fails to show a positive change over the next 28 days, indicating a decoupling of these activities.

mechanism_narrative: The rapid decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, coupled with increases across all other categories, indicates a relaxation of stay-at-home recommendations or mandates. This policy shift directly encourages out-of-home activities, leading to an immediate boost in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 7 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining low or decreasing further, suggesting policy effects are saturated or overridden.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks indicates a fundamental shift in daily routines, with people spending less time at home and more time engaging in out-of-home activities, which will continue to benefit RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent recovery of GROCERY_PHARM mobility, now nearing the -9% baseline, suggests a return to more regular shopping patterns and increased comfort with public spaces. This increased foot traffic in essential retail will spill over into adjacent retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM sustains above -10% for at least one week
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains above -10% but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days, indicating a lack of spillover effect.

mechanism_narrative: The high and recently increasing PARKS mobility, combined with the general upward trend in RETAIL_REC, suggests favorable weather conditions are encouraging outdoor activities. This positive sentiment and increased outdoor presence will likely extend to nearby retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains above 50% and RETAIL_REC is increasing
failure_condition: Despite high PARKS mobility and increasing RETAIL_REC, RETAIL_REC declines over the next 14 days, suggesting other factors are overriding seasonal effects.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and significant recovery across all mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) indicates a broad societal shift towards pre-pandemic activity levels. This collective return to normalcy will sustain the upward trajectory of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The collective upward trend across these mobility categories reverses, or RETAIL_REC specifically fails to improve over the next 28 days, indicating a halt in the recovery.
